Definition: from G1223 and G5101; through what cause?, i.e. why?:--wherefore, why.
BiblicalUsage: These are two words standing together, through and what, and the Greek text never joins them into a single word. The Pharisees ask why Jesus eats with publicans and sinners, and the same two words ask the question again in Luke, and in both places the question is why.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that why is the question the Pharisees never got past; they asked why Jesus ate with sinners, and the answer is the gospel itself: He came to call sinners, not the righteous, to repentance.
